rationale: X accurately traces both branches of `content_for`, including capture selection, ordered append versus `flush` replacement, nil write returns, blank read behavior, `content_for?`, and the SafeBuffer path from capture through storage and layout insertion. These claims match actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/capture_helper.rb:47-65 and 172-217, actionview/lib/action_view/flows.rb:9-27, and actionview/lib/action_view/buffers.rb:45-79; `actionview/bin/test test/template/capture_helper_test.rb` also passed with 27 runs and 68 assertions. Apart from one minor ERB-tag explanation issue, X is comprehensive and at parity with the references without a material error.
shortcomings: X says the nil write return prevents `<% content_for :x do %>` from leaking output, but a non-output `<% %>` tag would not emit the method return anyway; nil matters for `<%= content_for ... %>`, while the temporary raw-buffer swap in actionview/lib/action_view/buffers.rb:72-79 is what prevents captured block bytes from entering the parent buffer. R1 states this distinction more precisely.
